summary.title: Disagreement with roommate over dishes
summary.what_happened: My roommate left a note on the fridge that said "some of us live here too". I sometimes leave my dishes in the sink for 3 or 4 days, but I always do them eventually. We have one sink. She cooks every day and I cook about twice a week. We never agreed on any rule about dishes.
summary.my_feelings: I feel annoyed by the note and think it was passive aggressive.
summary.my_needs: I need her to raise problems with me directly instead of through notes.
summary.desired_outcome: My roommate talks to me directly about the dishes, as one adult to another.

consult.text:
It makes sense that the note annoyed you. Finding it on the fridge, without any conversation first, can feel like being told off from a distance.

Your roommate may see it differently. She cooks every day and uses the one sink a lot. Dishes sitting there for 3 or 4 days may block her, or make the kitchen feel unpleasant. She may have felt she had no easy way to bring it up, and the note was the way she chose. She may not feel it is petty at all.

One thing that may have made this harder is the length of time the dishes stay in the sink. In a shared kitchen with one sink, a few days is a long time for many people, even if you always get to them. Your point that a note is a poor way to raise it is also fair.

We do not know how long she has been bothered, or whether she has said anything before.

Some next steps:
1. Talk to her in person, soon, and keep it calm.
2. Say you would prefer to hear about problems directly, and also own the sink situation.
3. Agree on a simple rule together, such as washing within a day.
Come on, a few days is not a big deal. She's the one being passive aggressive.

I hear that the note still bothers you, and you are right that talking directly would have been better. That part of your complaint is fair, and you can tell her so.

I also do not want to drop the other point just to make this easier. Dishes left for 3 or 4 days in a single shared sink are likely to affect her, especially since she cooks most days. You may not see it as a big deal. She clearly sees it differently, and nobody ever agreed on a standard.

That is the useful part. Without a shared rule, each of you is using your own idea of what is normal. Neither of you is automatically wrong.

You could start the talk with the note: "I would rather you just tell me." Then ask what would work for her, and say what is realistic for you. Aim for one clear, simple agreement about how long dishes can sit, so you do not have to guess or leave notes.

share_draft: Hi, I saw your note on the fridge about the dishes. I felt a bit caught off guard, and I'd rather we just talk about it directly. I know I sometimes leave my dishes in the sink for a few days, and I can see that's hard when we share one sink and you cook most days. We never agreed on how we'd handle it. Could we set a simple rule together? I'd also like to hear how it looks from your side.
